parts.markdown:
Use our free **Alabama paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Alabama income tax, Social Security, Medicare and applicable local occupational taxes.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your pay frequency and customize your payroll deductions to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Whether you work in Birmingham, Huntsville, Montgomery, Mobile or another Alabama community, knowing your estimated net income can help you compare salary offers, prepare a monthly budget and make informed financial decisions.

## How to Use the Alabama Paycheck Calculator

Start by selecting the type of income you receive.

Salaried employees should enter their annual compensation before taxes. Hourly employees should enter their hourly rate, regular working hours and qualifying overtime hours.

Next, select your payment frequency. Enter federal and Alabama income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Add retirement contributions, health insurance premiums, additional withholding and other employee deductions where appropriate.

If your employer deducts a municipal or county occupational tax, enter the total withheld for the pay period.

The calculator estimates individual deductions and displays your remaining net income.

For more accurate results, use your most recent pay stub and withholding certificates when completing the inputs.

Employers must first account for relevant deductions and exemptions using the official withholding procedure.

Review the [Alabama Department of Revenue withholding guidance](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/tax-types/income-tax-withholding/) for additional information.

## Alabama Standard Deductions and Withholding Exemptions

Alabama's withholding calculation differs from simpler flat-rate state tax systems.

The standard deduction can vary according to annualized earnings and the employee's withholding classification.

For example, the standard deduction for an employee claiming single exemption may decrease as annualized wages rise.

The calculation can also account for personal exemptions, dependent exemptions and an applicable federal income tax deduction.

These adjustments mean that multiplying gross pay by 5% will not necessarily provide an accurate estimate of Alabama income tax withholding.

Our Alabama salary calculator uses the withholding amounts shown on your pay stub.

The [2026 Alabama withholding tax booklet](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/whbooklet_0126.pdf) contains the official calculation instructions.

## Understanding Alabama Occupational Taxes

Some Alabama municipalities and counties impose occupational taxes on qualifying employment earnings.

These taxes may apply because of the location where you perform your work rather than simply the location where you live.

Consequently, two employees earning identical salaries may receive different net pay when their employment locations are subject to different occupational tax requirements.

For illustration, suppose your applicable occupational tax rate is 1% and you receive $2,500 in earnings fully subject to that tax.

The occupational tax would be:

$2,500 × 0.01 = $25

This is a hypothetical example rather than a rate applicable to every Alabama municipality.

To confirm a local tax rate, check with your employer or municipal government.

Workers in Birmingham can consult the [City of Birmingham](https://www.birminghamal.gov/) for local tax information.

Remote workers and employees working across multiple municipalities may require additional calculations.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Alabama Paychecks

### Federal income tax

Federal withholding depends on your taxable earnings, payment frequency, filing status and Form W-4 information.

Employees with more than one job, working spouses or other income may require additional withholding adjustments.

The official [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) explains federal payroll withholding methods.

### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages toward Social Security.

For 2026, the annual taxable wage ceiling is $184,500.

An employee receiving $2,500 in covered wages who has not reached the annual limit would contribute $155.

### Medicare

Ordinary Medicare withholding is 1.45% of covered employee earnings.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% on Medicare wages exceeding $200,000 paid by that employer during the calendar year.

The final Additional Medicare Tax liability may depend on your filing status.

Learn more through the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15).

## Alabama Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

An employee earning $65,000 annually would generally receive the following gross payments.

Assuming a $2,500 biweekly paycheck is fully subject to ordinary federal payroll contributions:

Social Security: $155.00

Medicare: $36.25

Total: $191.25

Approximately $2,308.75 remains before federal income tax, Alabama income tax, occupational taxes and other employee deductions.

If a hypothetical occupational tax of 1% also applies to the full paycheck, another $25 would be deducted.

Use your actual withholding information in the calculator to obtain a more complete take-home pay estimate.

## Alabama Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly workers can estimate their gross earnings using their wage and hours worked.

Suppose an Alabama employee earns $24 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus five qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$24 × 40 = $960

Overtime earnings:

$24 × 1.5 × 5 = $180

Total gross pay:

$1,140

Applicable payroll taxes and deductions are then calculated from the relevant taxable wage amounts.

Not every employee qualifies for overtime. Check the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) if you are uncertain about your employment classification.

Alabama employees should not assume that previous temporary state overtime tax exemptions continue to apply to current wages.

## Retirement Contributions and Other Payroll Deductions

Your paycheck may include deductions for retirement plans, healthcare, dental insurance and other benefits.

Traditional 401(k) contributions generally reduce current federal income-taxable wages. Roth retirement contributions generally do not provide the same immediate income tax reduction.

Certain employer-sponsored health insurance premiums may reduce some taxable wage amounts.

However, deductions do not necessarily receive identical treatment for federal income tax, Alabama income tax, Social Security and Medicare.

Check your pay stub and benefit documents to identify the appropriate deduction classification.

An employer with generous retirement matching and affordable healthcare benefits may offer better overall compensation even when the gross salary is lower than competing offers.

## Comparing Job Offers in Alabama

When evaluating employment opportunities, compare estimated take-home income rather than gross compensation alone.

For example, a salary increase from $60,000 to $70,000 represents approximately $833.33 in additional gross monthly income.

The actual increase in spending power will depend on taxes, retirement contributions, healthcare premiums and commuting expenses.

A position in Huntsville may involve different housing and transportation expenses from a position in Mobile or Montgomery.

Use the calculator to compare both salaries with the appropriate employment locations and withholding settings.

You can then use our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) and [debt-to-income ratio calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate how much financial flexibility each job could provide.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the Alabama income tax rate?

Alabama applies progressive individual income tax rates of 2%, 4% and 5%. Applicable deductions, exemptions and withholding classifications determine the actual amount deducted from your paycheck.

### Does Alabama have local payroll taxes?

Some Alabama municipalities and counties impose occupational taxes on qualifying employee earnings. Check the rules for your actual employment location before calculating local deductions.

### Why does my Alabama paycheck differ from the calculator?

Differences may arise from withholding elections, taxable wage definitions, local taxes, benefit deductions, irregular payments and payroll rounding. Compare your inputs with your employer's payroll records.
